dog.description_text: Bear - 3 years & 61lbs, Lab/Anatolian Mix, Neutered This dog is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Their foster says: "Bear is exactly what his name suggests: a big, lovable teddy bear who would happily spend his days curled up next to you. When he isn’t asking for cuddles, you’ll usually find him curled up like a little donut on a soft bed or couch, taking one of his many naps. At night, he loves sleeping right by your side, and in the morning, he is more than happy to roll over for belly rubs. He has a wonderful balance of playful and relaxed, making him a great companion for someone who wants a dog who enjoys both adventures and cozy days at home. He is also a fast learner and has already picked up several commands, including sit, lay down, and place. He is currently working on learning his name, and with his ability to learn quickly, I think he will continue making great progress with consistent training. He is comfortable being left alone and has had free range of the house without displaying destructive or mouthy behavior. One of the cutest things about Bear is how curious he is about the world around him. He absolutely loves looking at his own reflection, whether it’s in a mirror, a window, or even a puddle! He is also a true social butterfly and has been fantastic with dogs of all sizes and ages. Despite being a big boy, Bear still very much thinks he’s a puppy. He loves to play, roll around, and wrestle with his canine friends before eventually settling down for a nap. Because he enjoys canine companionship so much, he could be especially happy in a home with another friendly dog, ideally one who enjoys playing with a bigger dog. Bear is still figuring out the world of toys. He is not particularly interested in squeaky toys but enjoys soft plush toys and balls. If you approach him while he is relaxing, do not be surprised if he immediately rolls onto his back, belly up, asking for scratches. He also loves having his floppy ears cleaned and is very comfortable being handled. Overall, Bear is a sweet, affectionate, goofy, and loving companion who has so much love to give. He would make a wonderful addition to a home looking for a big cuddle bug with a playful side and a heart just as big as he is." Level of dog ownership experience required: INTERMEDIATE – This dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.) Energy level: Bear is a low-to-medium-energy dog who is perfectly happy lounging around the house for much of the day, but he also enjoys going on long walks and exploring. He is a BIG sniffer and wants to investigate every interesting spot along the way. He also loves bird-watching and gets especially curious when he spots one outside. He is adjusting to city life, although I think he would really thrive in a quieter suburban home where he could enjoy peaceful time indoors and ideally have a yard to stretch his legs. Okay in the city? We don’t know yet because this pup is brand new to us. Most adult dogs do well in the city after they’ve had time to adjust to a new environment, but some never adapt and need homes in the burbs. One thing to keep in mind is that he can be nervous around blow dryers and similar loud noises. On the other hand, he is an expert in the car and does not mind long drives, happily settling down for the ride. Potty trained? Bear is potty trained and has not had any accidents in the house. Social with other dogs? Yes, but we don’t know to what degree yet. Some like to wrestle with every passing pup, others can coexist well but prefer to keep to themselves. We’ll learn more soon. Social with cats? Not sure yet! Some breed mixes that are generally NOT great matches for homes with cats include large hounds, huskies, and shepherds. Jumping on people to say hello: When meeting new people, Bear is super friendly and greets them with a big tail wag from his VERY curly tail. He may get excited and jump up to give face kisses, so he would benefit from continued practice with polite greetings. Leash manners: Bear is still working on his leash skills, as he has not had much experience walking on a leash. He can pull at the beginning of a walk, especially when something exciting catches his attention, but once he gets some of that initial energy out, he settles into a much calmer walk and responds to corrections. He is already making progress and just needs someone patient and consistent who is willing to keep helping him learn. Cuddle bug level: He is the ultimate cuddle bug and, given the chance, will put his big head right in your lap for some love and attention. Comfortable with children? (ALWAYS requires adult supervision) : He is good with children and enjoys approaching them for a sniff and some pets, although because of his size and enthusiasm, he would be best suited to a family with children who are comfortable around a big dog who may accidentally knock them over. Medical status: Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies vaccines; heartworm tested if coming from Tennessee or Puerto Rico; spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake How did this dog end up with Social Tees? Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses. This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes. LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc
